validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated project. This is Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline, LLC's (KMLP) 'Lake Charles Expansion Project,' FERC Docket No. CP14-511 -- an NGA sec.7 application filed June 30, 2014 (per the FEIS Executive Summary, energy.gov/EIS-0498) to modify KMLP's existing 133-mile, 42-inch, Sabine Pass-originating pipeline system with a new north-to-south, bi-directional transportation path so it can deliver feed gas to the proposed Magnolia LNG export terminal at Lake Charles, LA. FERC's Aug 18, 2014 Notice of Intent to prepare an EIS (federalregister.gov/2014-19464) confirms the docket was already active by then and independently states the same 1,400 Mcf/d capacity and interconnect/header-pipe scope. The project was certificated by FERC's April 15, 2016 order (155 FERC 61,033, reh'g denied 157 FERC 61,149, both cited in the 2020 extension notice). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- an interstate NGA sec.7 transmission pipeline modification (EIA workbook: Pipeline Type='Interstate', Authority='FERC'), filed jointly with, but legally and financially distinct from, Magnolia LNG's NGA sec.3 terminal application (Docket CP14-347) -- KMLP's construction is explicitly conditioned on Magnolia LNG achieving FID (per the 2020 extension notice: 'KMLP states that construction of the Lake Charles Expansion Project is dependent upon Magnolia achieving FID'), which as of the most recent evidence (Jan 15, 2026 extension filing, federalregister.gov/2026-03548) has still not occurred -- Magnolia's non-FTA DOE export authorization is still pending after DOE required it to lapse and be refiled in Nov 2023. DUPLICATE: ruled out against P5881 ('Magnolia Intrastate Pipeline' in this batch's Haynesville-corridor duplicate-family list) -- EIA's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' sheet shows P5881 is an unrelated American Midstream project in Mississippi/Alabama (45 mi, 500 MMcf/d, On Hold), with zero geographic or corporate overlap with KMLP's Louisiana project (see cross_row_leads). Not a duplicate of any other Haynesville-corridor row (P5115/P6843/P0285/P2523/P7807/P7808/P7831/P7832/P2737) either -- those interconnect Haynesville production into various Gillis-hub trunklines, whereas P2559 is specifically KMLP's own import-terminal-to-LNG-terminal reversal at Lake Charles, ~50 mi west of the Gillis hub cluster; no shared termini found. ATTRIBUTION: Owner=Operator=KMLP (Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline Co LLC), 100%, uncontested -- the FEIS states the facilities 'would be constructed, owned, and operated by KMLP,' and EIA's 'Pipeline Operator Name' field independently agrees. LOCATION: Louisiana/Louisiana correct -- FEIS specifies Acadia, Calcasieu, and Evangeline Parishes, LA; EIA's State(s)/Beg_State/End_State all = LA. No route geometry exists in the routes repo for P2559 (geometry: null), so no route-vs-sheet mismatch to evaluate.

validity.researcher_notes: EIA's current, dedicated Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook classifies this exact row as Project Type='Reversal' with Miles=0 and Diameter blank -- filled as such below (Length [ref] REFS_ADDED, Diameter [ref] UNRESOLVED). However, the original 2014 FERC application (as described in both the Aug 2014 Federal Register NOI and the 2015 FEIS) documents genuine NEW pipe construction, not merely a flow-direction reversal of existing pipe: 'approximately 40 feet of 36-inch-diameter pipeline' (new interconnect riser off KMLP's existing 42-inch mainline), 'approximately 6,400 feet of 36-inch-diameter and 700 feet of 24-inch-diameter header pipelines' (2014-19464), and the FEIS separately states the low-pressure header alone is '1.2-mile-long' / 36-inch and affects 20.7 acres, with the high-pressure header '700-foot-long, 24-inch-diameter.' Summed, this is roughly 7,140 ft (~1.35 route-miles) of mixed 36-in/24-in new pipe -- a real, sourced figure, but I am not asserting it as the sheet's Length/Diameter because (a) it would require summing several distinct segment figures myself rather than citing one authoritative total, (b) it is unclear whether GEM's convention for a 'reversal' project type wants this granularity captured at all given the hard rule that an expansion with no new physical pipe gets Length=0, and this project sits ambiguously between 'reversal of existing capacity' and 'construction of new short segments,' and (c) EIA's own dedicated, currently-maintained dataset -- which is otherwise an exact match on Capacity and SegmentCost for this row -- affirmatively classifies it as Miles=0. Recommend a human researcher weigh whether to record the ~1.2-1.35 mi / 36-24 in figure instead.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a Delayed rather than Shelved situation, and Status=proposed remains the correct GEM value: as recently as Jan 15, 2026 (the most current dated evidence found, seven months before this sweep) the applicant AFFIRMATIVELY requested a further extension rather than letting the certificate lapse or withdrawing -- the opposite signal from a dormant/abandoned project. The one nuance worth flagging: the Feb 2026 Federal Register notice's body text names only 'Magnolia' (the LNG terminal applicant) explicitly requesting the extension, while KMLP's own pipeline docket (CP14-511-001) appears only in the docket-number header, not restated in prose -- i.e., this notice speaks most directly to the TERMINAL's timeline. I bridge this via EIA's independent Notes field, which explicitly states the same Jan 2026 filing covers 'both the terminal and the pipeline reversal' (consistent with the 2020 extension notice, which was filed jointly by Magnolia AND KMLP under all three dockets, CP14-347/CP19-19/CP14-511, together). Dormancy check: even setting aside the 2026 filing, the pattern of continuous, timely extension requests since 2016 (2020 request before the 2021 deadline; 2026 request before the [inferred] 2026 deadline) shows active management of the certificate, not silence -- so neither the 2-year-no-progress-→-shelved nor the 4-year-→-cancelled dormancy thresholds are triggered. No ShelvedCancelledType change needed.
